CLAUDEGM.Help.Gm:
Claude GM — help

Commands

  • /claude <request> — ask Claude something about the open world.
  • /claude! <request> — strongest model, more effort (session prep, big tasks).
  • /ai (or /ia) <question> — fast, cheap model for simple questions.
  • /claude undo — reverts everything the last request changed (shows the list first).
  • /claude undo clear — erases the undo history (changes nothing in the world).
  • /claude stop — stops the request in progress.
  • /claude reset (or new) — Claude forgets the conversation and starts over.
  • /claude panel — opens Claude's window.
  • /claude status — shows the configuration.
  • /claude summary (or sheet) — instant summary of the selected tokens (or of the sheet in focus in the panel): HP, AC, spell slots, uses, conditions.
  • /claude queue — shows who is waiting; /claude clear queue removes players' questions from the queue.

Every command also works with its Portuguese alias (ajuda, status, painel, resumo, parar, nova, fila, limpar fila, desfazer, desfazer limpar).

Where to click

  • Robot in the token controls (left bar): opens the panel. In the panel, start with ! (strong) or ? (quick).
  • Robot in the header of actor, item, journal and scene sheets: opens the panel with that document in focus, with quick actions.
  • Robot in the token HUD (right click on a token): the same, for that token.

What Claude does

  • Look things up: world documents and sheets (with computed AC, modifiers and DCs), compendiums, journal text, the session chat.
  • Create and change: documents (actors, items, journals, scenes...), compendium imports, dice rolls and chat messages.

Safety

  • Changes ask for your approval (configurable); public chat messages always do.
  • Everything Claude creates or changes can be undone with /claude undo (the last 30 requests, even after a reload).
  • Players cannot see your conversations with Claude.

Players

With "Players can ask" on, players use /claude only for questions about their own character: sheet, the rules that apply and their story as recorded. Claude only reads the characters the player owns, the journals shared with them and the rules in compendiums; it refuses campaign lore, monsters, NPCs and secrets, never makes things up, changes nothing, and accepts 1 question every 15 s (20 per hour). They also have /claude summary (instant, no AI). Questions go into a queue and are answered one at a time; your requests go first. You see every question and answer.

Examples

  • /claude find the goblin boss in the compendiums and create a tougher version called Grukk
  • /claude summarize tonight's session from the chat log
  • /claude create a journal entry with the rumors heard at the tavern
  • /claude! write a journal for the players with what happened this session
  • /ia what is the goblin's AC?
CLAUDEGM.Help.Player:
Claude — help for players

Use /claude <question> to ask about your character.

Shortcuts

  • /claude summary (or sheet) — HP, AC, spell slots, remaining uses, conditions and coins, instantly (costs nothing).
  • /claude reset (or new) — starts a new conversation.

The commands also work with Portuguese aliases (ajuda, resumo, ficha, nova, limpar).

You can ask

  • Sheet numbers: abilities, skills, saves, AC, HP, speed, proficiencies.
  • Your spells, items, features and feats: what they do, how to use them, costs, recharges, DCs.
  • Rules that apply to something on your sheet (e.g. "how does my Sneak Attack work?"), and tactics with what you have.
  • Your character's story, as recorded on the sheet and in the journals the GM shared with you (e.g. "who is my character's father?"). If it is not recorded, Claude does not make it up.

You cannot

  • Campaign lore beyond what you have already received, NPCs, monsters, maps, secrets, chances of beating someone or what will happen — that is for the GM.
  • Change the sheet: Claude only reads.

The answer arrives in the chat only for you and the GM. The GM sees every question. If other players ask at the same time, yours goes into a queue and you see your position. One question at a time; limit of 1 every 15 s and 20 per hour.
